subject: Dedicated capacity rate warranty & measurement runbook
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <procurement@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions — throughput warranty and acceptance

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the overview earlier. Procurement needs a concrete measurement methodology we can share with our infra team so Legal can sign off on the throughput warranty. Specifically we need to confirm: tokens/sec vs requests/sec definitions, latency targets (p50/p95/p99), what constitutes a failed run, and the measurement harness we will run (customer infra vs Redwood-hosted runner).

Acme's asks are:
- A baseline tokens/sec guarantee for our 12x GPU reserved commit at the 8k context size workload.
- A latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms for single-request path for the default model variant.
- Clear pass/fail and credit calculation for missed SLA windows.
- A 30-day acceptance window to validate throughput after deployment (we can provide recorded traffic or run a synthetic harness).

We are also evaluating discounts tied to the warranty — if Redwood accepts the above measurement plan and warranty, Acme is prepared to sign a 12-month reserved commit at the suggested 20% list discount.

Can you send a proposed test plan and sample measurement scripts we can run (or let you run) next week? We need to keep this lightweight — legal wants objective evidence, not lengthy back-and-forth.

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Procurement, Acme Enterprises

Attachment: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions — throughput warranty and acceptance

Hi Sofia / Tom,

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise runbook + measurement harness we propose for validation (see acme_performance_run_spec.xlsx and measurement_harness.sh). High level summary below so Legal/Infra can review quickly:

1) Measurement definitions
- tokens_per_second: aggregate number of generated tokens divided by effective test time excluding warm-up (we report both aggregate and per-GPU normalized values).
- requests_per_second: completed request count / effective test time. For batch requests we report both raw request RPS and token-weighted RPS.
- latency: measured end-to-end server-side latency per request; we report p50/p95/p99 over the effective window.

2) Test harness and runner options
- Option A (recommended): Redwood-managed runner in our dedicated lab that mirrors the production serving stack. Pros: identical runtime, consistent KV cache behavior, deterministic tooling. Cons: requires limited network access for results export.
- Option B: Customer-hosted runner (Acme). We will provide the same harness scripts (measurement_harness.sh) and guidance for environment parity. Runs must use the provided sample_payloads.json to replicate request distribution.

3) Warm-up / effective window
- 10 minute warm-up at the target concurrency + batch settings to populate KV caches and stabilize compilers.
- 60 minute effective measurement window. We report minute-by-minute metrics and a final aggregated result.

4) Acceptance criteria (example for 12x GPU / 8k context)
- Aggregate tokens_per_second >= 1,200,000 tokens/sec (measured across the 60m window).
- p95 latency <= 450ms; p99 latency <= 900ms.
- Failure: if either metric misses the target for >10% of the 60 minute windows (i.e., more than 6 of the minute buckets), the run is considered failed.

5) Credits and remediation
- Single failed acceptance run triggers a remediation plan and a repeat run within 7 calendar days.
- If repeat run also fails, Redwood will issue service credits equal to 10% of the monthly reserved commit for the first missed run. Persistent misses (2+ failed repeat runs) escalate to a contract-level liquidity discussion.

6) Edge conditions we will control for
- We will fix model version, sequence length distribution (sample_payloads.json), and quantization profile. If Acme needs alternative model variants, those are a separate measurement run.
- We exclude operator-induced throttling and network outages from the measurement (both parties will annotate incidents).

Commercial proposal:
- Standard offer: 12-month reserved commit (12x GPU pool) with 20% list discount conditional on passing acceptance run within the 30-day window.
- If Acme prefers a staged commit, we can offer a 15% discount for a 6-month ramp with acceptance in the first 30 days.
- Any additional discount request (greater than 20%) requires approval from Sales leadership.

Next steps:
- If this approach looks acceptable, we can schedule a test window next Tuesday (2027-07-06) or run Redwood-managed tests the week after. I attached the run_spec and harness scripts.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_performance_run_spec.xlsx, measurement_harness.sh, sample_payloads.json
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity questions — throughput warranty and acceptance

Kim / Marissa — quick internal note before we lock in dates with Acme. Couple of suggested tweaks to reduce commercial exposure:

- Reduce effective window from 60m to 30m but require two independent 30m runs on separate days (this lowers variability impact while keeping time reasonable).
- Add a clause: if model patching or minor infra compilers are applied by Redwood during the 30-day acceptance window, Acme can request a single re-run (no additional credits).
- For the credit schedule, propose a stepped credit: 7% monthly credit for one failed run, 15% for repeated failure. That avoids opening to a flat 10% on first miss — finance will prefer gradation.

Also recommend we pre-authorize a 22% max discount in writing but require Sales leadership sign-off for anything above 20% during contracting. Aditya — can you confirm approval to hold 22% as our negotiation ceiling for this enterprise opportunity?

If you agree, Kimberly I think we can commit to Redwood-managed runs and propose July 6 for run 1, July 8 for run 2. Acme can elect to run customer-hosted too; we just need identical harness and to sign off on the results.

—Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
